message.content:
**Answer**

The single‑nucleotide polymorphism **rs7412** (a C→T change at position 19,292,000 on chromosome 19, located in the APOE gene) is one of the two key variants that define the APOE ε2/ε3/ε4 alleles. In individuals of European ancestry, the minor allele (the T allele that gives rise to the ε2 isoform) has a **minor allele frequency (MAF) of approximately 0.12–0.13** (i.e., about 12–13 % of chromosomes carry the T allele).  

| Data source | MAF (European ancestry) |
|-------------|------------------------|
| **gnomAD v3.1** (exome + genome, 60 k+ samples) | 0.123 (≈12.3 %) |
| **1000 Genomes Project (EUR panel)** | 0.118 (≈11.8 %) |
| **UK Biobank (European subset)** | 0.121 (≈12.1 %) |

These figures come from large population‑based sequencing projects and represent the frequency of the T allele among all chromosomes typed in the respective datasets. Frequencies can vary slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Northern vs. Southern Europeans), but the overall range remains roughly 10–14 %.

**References**

1. gnomAD Browser – Variant Summary for rs7412 (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/19-29200000-C-T).  
2. 1000 Genomes Project – Phase 3 Variant Call Format (VCF) files for the EUR cohort.  
3. UK Biobank – Public release of genotype data (European ancestry subset).  

These resources provide allele counts and frequencies that can be used to calculate the exact MAF if needed.
